case_name: Prem Prakash @ Lillu & Anr. v State Of Haryana
respondent:
State Of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

7 July 2011
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 91 OF 2007
The Judgment was delivered by : Swatanter Kumar, J.
1.  Three accused, namely Dharambir @ Pappu, Prem Prakash @ Lillu and Herchand @ Poley, were charged for an offence punishable u/ss. 366 and 376(2)(g) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the 'IPC'). Upon trial, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Rohtak, by judgment and order dated 31st July, 1992 held all the three accused guilty of the offences of kidnapping and gang rape of Kumari Sudesh and, thus, they were sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment of 10 years with a fine of Rs.500/ -each. In case of default of payment of fine, they were ordered to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a further period of one month.

facts: Three accused, namely Dharambir @ Pappu, Prem Prakash @ Lillu and Herchand @ Poley, were charged for an offence punishable under ss. 366 and 376(2)(g) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The accused were sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment of 10 years with a fine of Rs.500/- each.
The accused preferred an appeal before the High Court, which was dismissed vide its judgment dated 27th July, 2005.
One of the accused, Prem Prakash @ Lillu had expired during the pendency of the appeal before this Court.
issues: Whether the accused were guilty of the offence with which they were charged?
Whether the prosecution's case was reliable and trustworthy?
petitioner_arguments: The accused argued that there were contradictions in the statements of the witnesses.

They denied the incident in its entirety and took a specific stand that Pratap Singh, father of Kumari Sudesh was carrying on cultivation on the land belonging to the family of the accused and since he had stopped them from carrying on the agricultural activity, Pratap Singh had developed animosity towards them.
Prem Prakash @ Lillu argued that he was not named in the FIR and has been falsely implicated.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution argued that the accused were guilty of the offence with which they were charged.
They contended that there were no contradictions in the statements of the witnesses that would affect the merits of the case.
court_reasoning: The trial court found that the accused were guilty of the offence with which they were charged.

The Court observed that some discrepancies had been pointed out between the statements of the prosecution witnesses, but these were not significant and did not render the statement of the prosecutrix unreliable or untrustworthy.
holding: The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal and upheld the conviction of the accused.
The Court held that there was no reason to disbelieve the version given by the prosecutrix.
